README.md.excerpt:
pstack — standalone mirror

Mirror of cursor/plugins/pstack by Poteto — kept in sync for standalone use. Sponsored by Plannotator.

Poteto's Bro Skill was created by me, backnotprop/bro

## Install pstack is a folder of plain [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) (`skills//SKILL.md`). You don't need [Cursor](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack). The [`skills` CLI](https://skills.sh) installs them into Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Cursor, OpenCode, and other agents: ```bash npx skills add backnotprop/pstack ``` The CLI shows every skill in a list you can search. Select the skills you want, then select your agents. ## Skills Cursor's original README is [further down this page](#pstack). These skills don't call other pstack skills, so each one works alone: `unslop`, `bro`, `how`, `why`, `tdd`, `typescript-best-practices`, `arena`, `swarm`, `interrogate`, `reflect`, `show-me-your-work`, `figure-it-out`, `automate-me`, `correct`, `benchmark-checklist`, `in-your-own-words`, `sharpen`, `reframe`, `statechart` Some skills call other skills. Install these together: | Skill | Also install | |---|---| | `teach` | `how`, `why` | | `technical-writing` | `unslop` | | `architect` | `arena` | | `blast-radius` | `arena`, `how`, `why`, `unslop` | | `create-verification-skill` | `maintain-verification-skill` | | `create-formal-verification-skill` | `maintain-formal-verification-skill`, `statechart` | | `ketchup` | `bro` | | `ketchup-video` | `ketchup`, `bro` | | `poteto-mode` | all `principle-*` skills and most of the other skills | | `poteto-help` | the skills you want help with | Skills that spawn subagents point to the Subagents section of `poteto-mode` to pick each subagent's effort. Without `poteto-mode`, they use the default effort. ## What this mirror changes Many skills were Cursor-specific. They've been rewritten to work in any harness. Codex ignores the `disable-model-invocation: true` mark that keeps most pstack skills from running unless you call them. So each marked skill also gets an `agents/openai.yaml` that tells Codex the same thing. The skill stays out of Codex's startup prompt, and `$skill` still runs it. ([#26](https://github.com/backnotprop/pstack/issues/26)) The mirror also carries two community fixes that aren't upstream yet: - `no-comments` keeps a comment about an outside rule (a dependency, platform, or protocol) when it can't check the rule, and marks it for review instead of deleting it. A rejected review no longer stops the whole run. ([#14](https://github.com/backnotprop/pstack/issues/14)) - `watch-pr` no longer adds a pull request from a fork to a watched stack, so a fork's review comments stay out of the agent's context, and it strips control characters from review paths, authors and comment text before printing them. Patch from [cursor/plugins#1194](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/pull/1194). ([cursor/plugins#1193](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/issues/1193)) --- # pstack [See Pstack Blog](https://x.com/poteto/article/2094457600259842065?lang=en) i'm [poteto](https://x.com/poteto). i'm not a president or ceo, but i've worked with millions of lines of code at Meta, Netflix, and Cursor. i'm also on the react core team where i help build and maintain react compiler. there's a growing sense that ai writes too much slop code. i agree. i don't want to ship like a team of twenty slop artists. throughput without quality is not a goal i aspire to. if you want to go fast, go deep first. **pstack is my answer.** these are the same skills i use every day to ship high quality code at Cursor. this turns cursor into a real engineering team. the goal is not to maximize loc, in fact it's the opposite. pstack helps you write less, but higher quality code. **pstack gives you fearless parallelism.** when you can go deep on one agent and trust it to write good, verifiable code, you can truly parallelize with confidence. start multiple agents up with `poteto-mode` and trust that they'll apply rigorous engineering principles to their work. **cursor gives you the best of all worlds.** every frontier model has its strengths and weaknesses. use any model with pstack. in fact, many of my skills use multi-model workflows to take advantage of each model's unique strengths. fork it. improve it. make it yours. PRs are welcome! ## install ```bash /add-plugin pstack ``` in claude code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins /plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins ``` claude code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed.
